findings.test: PSM: OS >= PFS at every time point (no curve crossing)
findings.inputs: base-case PFS + OS curves over full (extrapolated) horizon
findings.expected: OS >= PFS at every time point (no curve crossing); occupancies partition to 1
findings.observed: PFS exceeds OS at 251/521 points (48%): two ranges -- t=1..10 wks (max excess 0.0011, early-curve noise) AND t=267..520 wks (254/521 = 49% of the ENTIRE horizon, max excess 0.0229) in the crp+ (experimental-arm) subgroup curve. crp- subgroup also crosses t=287..520 (234 wks, max excess 0.0024). At every clamped point, model_fun's pfs<-pmin(pfs,os) silently forces P (progressed) occupancy to exactly 0, so for roughly the back half of the 10-year horizon the crp arm's 'progressed' health state is eliminated by construction rather than by the fitted curve shape.
findings.location: scripts/R/functions/model_fun.R:376-382 (pfs_pos<-pmin(pfs_pos,os_pos), crp+); scripts/R/functions/prediction_functions.R:39-190 (generate_population_averaged_predictions, independent OS/PFS extrapolation per subgroup); scripts/R/analysis/06_parametric_survival_analysis.R (global best-fit: OS=weibull, PFS=lognormal, fit independently with no joint/ordering constraint)
findings.recommended_fix: Root cause: OS and PFS are fitted as two independently-parameterized flexsurvreg models (globally best-fit by AIC: OS=weibull, PFS=lognormal) with no constraint that PFS(t) <= OS(t) in the extrapolated tail. For the small crp+ subgroup (~15 patients: 45*0.338 pos), a lognormal PFS tail can decay slower than a weibull OS tail, crossing durably rather than momentarily. The current pmin(pfs,os) patch in model_fun.R only fixes this AT THE POINT OF USE (with a bare warning(), easy to miss), discarding the fitted PFS shape for essentially the whole second half of the horizon rather than fixing the extrapolation. Recommended: (1) fit PFS and OS with a structure that enforces stochastic ordering during extrapolation (e.g., model time-to-progression-or-death as OS and model 'progression given still at risk' as a separate hazard added to the OS hazard, or fit both endpoints jointly with a shared frailty/copula so PFS<=OS holds by construction); (2) short of a structural fix, cap extrapolation at the last observed follow-up time and apply a transparent, documented tail assumption beyond that point (CDA-AMC 21/22 -- flag and allow restricting the horizon to the observed-data period); (3) elevate the current warning() to a results-level flag reporting the % of the horizon and the biomarker subgroups affected by the clamp, since ~49% of the crp+ horizon is silently overridden.

findings.location: scripts/R/analysis/03_biomarker_strategies.R:24 (p_crp <- mean(data$crp, na.rm=TRUE), full data, n=74) vs scripts/R/functions/prediction_functions.R:164 (prevalence <- mean(...data_complete[[biomarker_name]]...), complete-case data, n=68)
findings.recommended_fix: Currently immaterial for the headline CEA numbers (model_fun.R never reads the *_weighted_OS/PFS fields for cost/QALY -- it recomputes the pos/neg weighting itself from params$p_crp, which correctly uses the full-data prevalence). BUT scripts/QMD/report/biomarker_decomposition.qmd:103-115 DOES read *_weighted_OS/PFS directly to report a 'Weighted' restricted-mean-survival life-years row, so that reported number uses a silently different (data_complete-based) prevalence than the CEA's own p_crp. Fix: make generate_population_averaged_predictions() take prevalence as a parameter (or read it from strategies_df/params) instead of recomputing it internally from data_complete, so the *_weighted_* curve field and l_params_base$p_crp are guaranteed to share one prevalence definition. This is a 'duplicate definition with drift' pattern (CHAOS/TECH-VER) -- currently ~0.02pp drift for CRP but ~0.8pp for TMB/BRAF (see BB-PSM-WCHECK-tmb_braf), and would grow if data completeness worsens.

Mortality := 0: nobody dies; undiscounted LY == horizon; LYs equal across arms
findings.expected: LY equal across arms; undisc LY == horizon; final dead occupancy == 0
findings.observed: With p_os forced to 1 everywhere (nobody dies), undiscounted LY = 10.0192y for every strategy (equal across arms, as expected) but the intended horizon is exactly 10y (time_horizon=520 weeks / 52). The 0.0192y (1.4 day) overstatement is systematic: the model evaluates state occupancy at 521 grid points t=0,1,...,520 inclusive (a length-(time_horizon+1) curve) and sums p_alive*cl over all 521 points with no half-cycle correction, i.e. it double-counts both endpoints of a 520-week span (521/52=10.0192 vs the intended 520/52=10.0000). This affects every strategy identically (confirmed: control=crp=tmb_braf=10.0192), so it does not distort INCREMENTAL comparisons or ICERs, but it systematically inflates every strategy's reported (undiscounted and discounted) life-years and QALYs by ~0.19%.
findings.location: scripts/R/functions/model_fun.R:97-98 (time_horizon default 520, expected_length=time_horizon+1); scripts/R/functions/calculate_outcomes.R:28-32 (qalys_undiscounted <- (p_pf*u_np+p_p*u_p)*cl, summed over all n_cycles=521 points with no half-cycle correction); scripts/R/analysis/02_setup_and_global_variables.R:22 (time_horizon<-520 'i.e. 10 years in weeks')
findings.recommended_fix: Downgraded from critical (template default) to minor: the effect is small (~0.19%), systematic across all strategies (does not reverse or materially distort ICERs, since it inflates both arms of every incremental comparison by essentially the same relative factor), and there is no cohort-conservation or ordering violation -- purely a grid-counting artifact from the absence of a half-cycle correction (or, equivalently, from treating a 520-week horizon as 521 evaluation points). Fix: either (a) apply a standard half-cycle correction (weight the first and last cycle's contribution by 0.5), or (b) drop the t=520 (521st) point from the summation so exactly 520 unit-length cycles are counted, or (c) explicitly document that the reported horizon is 521/52=10.019 years rather than 10 years. Any of these removes the artifact; (a) is the standard DARTH/CHEERS convention.

findings.test: Swap two arms' inputs: outputs swap
findings.inputs: control excluded (single-curve/no-prevalence arm, not swappable with a biomarker arm); all curve+prevalence inputs of crp and tmb_braf exchanged
findings.expected: control excluded (single-curve/no-prevalence arm, not swappable with a biomarker arm); results of crp and tmb_braf exchange exactly
findings.observed: QALYs swap EXACTLY (base crp=1.38424/tmb_braf=1.35303 -> swapped crp=1.35303/tmb_braf=1.38424), confirming the clinical-effect (survival curve + prevalence) swap logic is correct. Costs do NOT fully swap: swapped crp=58295.5 (expected ~=base tmb_braf=60797.5, off by -2502) and swapped tmb_braf=57527.8 (expected ~=base crp=55025.8, off by +2502). The ~2502 residual = c_test_NGS(2518) - c_test_blood(16) = 2502 (discounted at cycle 1), i.e. exactly the difference between the two biomarkers' diagnostic-test costs.
findings.location: scripts/R/functions/calculate_outcomes.R:46-53 (test_costs[1] += c_test_NGS or c_test_blood, branched on the literal string biomarker=='tmb_braf'/'crp' -- not on any property of the swapped curve/params data)
findings.recommended_fix: This is a genuine structural coupling, not a numeric bug: model_fun.R's loop over biomarkers_to_run always calls calculate_outcomes() with the LITERAL strategy name ('crp' or 'tmb_braf'), and calculate_outcomes.R hard-codes which diagnostic-test-cost field applies to which name. Swapping the CURVE DATA (params$p_os/p_pfs/prevalence) therefore does not swap the associated diagnostic-test cost, because that cost is attached to the strategy's IDENTITY, not to its data. This is arguably intentional (CRP and NGS really are different-cost diagnostic technologies that don't travel with the survival curves), but it means the strategy definitions are not purely data-driven, which is a maintenance risk if a future analyst assumes 'swap the curves' fully redefines a strategy. Recommended: either document this explicitly next to ALL_BIOMARKERS in model_configs.R, or refactor calculate_outcomes.R to take the biomarker test cost as a parameter looked up via a params-level mapping (e.g. params$c_test_biomarker[[biomarker]]) rather than an if/else on the biomarker name, so a full strategy swap (curves + prevalence + test cost) is achievable in one operation.

findings.inputs: crp acquisition cost += 1000 (bump_acq_cost(l,'crp',add) raises c_drug_nivo, shared by crp+ and tmb_braf+)
findings.expected: only cost(crp) increases; all QALY/LY identical
findings.observed: Bumping via c_drug_nivo (the only cost-hook available for 'crp', since there is no dedicated crp acquisition-cost field) correctly leaves control's cost unchanged (delta=0) and leaves ALL QALYs/LYs unchanged (delta=0, confirming acquisition cost has no effect on clinical outcomes, as expected) -- but it raises BOTH crp (+2445.19) AND tmb_braf (+2747.31), not crp alone, because c_drug_nivo is genuinely shared: both crp+ and tmb_braf+ subgroups receive the same nivolumab product (calculate_outcomes.R:37, drug_costs <- (l_nivo*c_drug_nivo + ...) for treatment_type=='experimental', which applies identically regardless of which biomarker selected the patient).
findings.location: scripts/R/functions/calculate_outcomes.R:35-41 (drug_costs formula uses a single shared params$c_drug_nivo for every 'experimental' treatment_type call, i.e. for both crp+ and tmb_braf+ subgroups)
findings.recommended_fix: Intentional/realistic (nivolumab pricing does not depend on which biomarker selected the patient for treatment), so this is not a defect in the base-case model. It IS a real limitation for sensitivity-analysis design: there is currently no way to vary nivolumab acquisition cost for one biomarker-guided strategy only (e.g. a 'biosimilar available only via CRP-guided pathway' scenario). If such a scenario is ever needed, add a per-strategy price multiplier (e.g. params$c_drug_nivo_mult[[strategy]], defaulting to 1) rather than overloading the single shared c_drug_nivo scalar.

findings.expected: Half-cycle correction ON gives lower total LY than OFF
findings.recommended_fix: Confirmed by inspection (grep for half-cycle/HCC logic in model_fun.R and calculate_outcomes.R: no matches) that this weekly-cycle (cl=1/52) PSM has no half-cycle-correction toggle -- occupancy is evaluated at integer week points with no HCC weighting. findings.test: Double the efficacy/safety difference: ~2x incremental effects
findings.expected: incremental QALY ratio ~ 2 (within 30%; nonlinearity must be explained)
findings.observed: Base incremental QALY (crp - control) = -0.0299 (crp is WORSE than control in the base case); doubling the crp/tmb_braf-vs-control curve deviation gives -0.0442, ratio 1.478 (outside the 30% band around 2x). This is very likely explained by two compounding nonlinearities in scale_effect_diff's construction: (1) the clamp01(control + k*(curve-control)) saturates at the [0,1] probability bounds for any point already close to 0 or 1 -- unavoidable for a probability-scale perturbation; (2) doubling the PFS/OS deviations pushes MORE of the horizon into the PFS>OS crossing region documented in BB-PSM-ORD-crp/tmb_braf, so model_fun's pmin(pfs,os) clamp discards an even larger, k-dependent share of the perturbed curve, adding a second source of nonlinearity on top of the intended effect-size scaling.
findings.location: validatehe_tests/blackbox_harness.R (scale_effect_diff setter, clamp01 bound) interacting with scripts/R/functions/model_fun.R:306-312/376-382/404-411 (pmin(pfs,os) clamp)
findings.recommended_fix: Not a standalone model defect -- flagging as a harness-test artifact compounded by the real BB-PSM-ORD crossing issue (see that finding's recommended_fix; fixing the OS/PFS extrapolation ordering there would likely also make this doubling test linearize better). If a cleaner DSA 2x/0.5x check is wanted independent of the crossing issue, scale the HAZARD (or a covariate coefficient) rather than the survival-probability curve directly, since probability-scale doubling is inherently nonlinear near [0,1] boundaries regardless of the crossing defect.
